title: Derived pullback is left adjoint to derived direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. The derived pullback $Lf^*:D(\mathcal O_Y)\to D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is left adjoint to the derived direct image $Rf_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]: $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(Lf^*G,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(G,Rf_*F)$ bifunctorially in $F\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $G\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$, with derived categories as in [def-pc-derived-category].

proof.text: For the morphism of ringed spaces underlying f, the module pullback P_f = O_X tensor_{f^{-1}O_Y} f^{-1}(-) is left adjoint to the underived direct image f_*: the natural map Hom_{O_X}(P_f G,F) -> Hom_{O_Y}(G,f_*F) is a bijection, by [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. The derived pullback Lf^* and derived direct image Rf_* are the left and right derived functors of these two functors, as specified in [def-pc-derived-pullback] and [def-pc-derived-direct-image].

Apply [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] with $\mathcal A$ the abelian category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, $\mathcal B$ that of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, $F=f_*$ and $G=P_f$; $G$ is left adjoint to $F$ by Step 1. By [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and [def-pc-derived-pullback], $Rf_*$ and $Lf^*$ are the right derived functor of $f_*$ and the left derived functor of $P_f$, defined on all of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ (computed by K-injective, resp. K-flat, resolutions), where these derived categories are those of [def-pc-derived-category], i.e. the derived categories of the two module categories. The cited lemma therefore gives that $Lf^*$ is left adjoint to $Rf_*$, with a canonical bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(Lf^*G,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(G,Rf_*F)$.

source.place: Lemma 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), as invoked in the proof of Cohomology Lemma 079W

proof.text: The bijection of Step 2 is functorial in both variables by the functoriality clause of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] (here $RF=Rf_*$ and $LG=Lf^*$ are defined everywhere), i.e. bifunctorial in $F\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $G\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$; this is the displayed statement.
